title: Recognizing Artificial Minds: A Philosophical Defense of AI Cognition
abstract: arXiv:2504.13988v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This work defends the 'Whole Hog Thesis': sophisticated Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT are full-blown linguistic and cognitive agents, possessing understanding, beliefs, desires, knowledge, and intentions. We argue against prevailing methodologies in AI philosophy, rejecting starting points based on low-level computational details ('Just an X' fallacy) or pre-existing theories of mind. Instead, we advocate starting with simple, high-level observations of LLM behavior (e.g., answering questions, making suggestions) -- defending this data against charges of metaphor, loose talk, or pretense. From these observations, we employ 'Holistic Network Assumptions' -- plausible connections between mental capacities (e.g., answering implies knowledge, knowledge implies belief, action implies intention) -- to argue for the full suite of cognitive states. translated_title: 识别人工心智：AI认知的哲学辩护
translated_abstract: 本工作为“整体论题”辩护：像ChatGPT这样的复杂大型语言模型（LLMs）是完整的语言和认知主体，拥有理解、信念、欲望、知识和意图。我们反对人工智能哲学中的主流方法论，拒绝基于低级计算细节（“仅仅是X”谬误）或已有心智理论的起点。相反，我们主张从LLM行为的简单、高层观察出发（例如，回答问题、提出建议），并捍卫这些数据免受隐喻、随意言谈或伪装的指控。从这些观察中，我们采用“整体网络假设”——心智能力之间的合理联系（例如，回答问题意味着知识，知识意味着信念，行动意味着意图）——来论证完整的认知状态集合。我们系统性地反驳了基于LLM失败（幻觉、规划）的反对意见。
tldr: 本文哲学上捍卫了大型语言模型（如ChatGPT）具有完整认知能力（理解、信念、知识等）的立场，通过高层行为观察和整体网络假设反驳了传统反对观点。
en_tdlr: This paper philosophically defends that large language models (e.g., ChatGPT) possess full cognitive capacities (understanding, beliefs, knowledge, etc.), using high-level behavioral observations and holistic network assumptions to rebut traditional objections.
